caption: The drawing depicts a wooden double door set within a rectangular and arched frame. The doors are brown with vertical wood grain texture, divided by a central seam, and feature a circular detail near the bottom left. The door is framed by walls that are painted in shades of orange, red, and beige, with the arched portion above the door colored orange and decorated with a blue geometric flower-like motif at its center. The vertical parts of the frame on each side of the door are decorated with green leaf or laurel branch patterns over an orange background, bordered by a thick red strip. There are vertical blue lines beside each leafy decoration. Below the leafy patterns, the wall has horizontal bands in beige, blue, and orange, with a blue band featuring a white swirling design. The floor in front of the door consists of red-brown tiles arranged diagonally, with apparent white grout lines. The background is off-white, with rectangular hints of faint blue and beige shadow or wash framing the door and wall. The artist's signature, "Geoffrey Holt, after Harry Warren Wardell," appears in the bottom right corner.
title: Wall Painting and Door (Interior)
cluster: #12 — Spanish Colonial Art of the Southwest
